Years ago, MacBooks included slots that allowed you to secure your computer to a desk leg or similar fixed object using a cable lock. This kind of design was most useful in coffee shops, so you wouldn't have to carry your laptop around when you went back to the counter to order another drink.

Those slots have long disappeared, but now you can buy an adapter to add a security feature to your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro...

You'd have to be a long-time MacBook user to remember the built-in security slot on the side of the chassis. Those slots were designed for T-shaped accessories that you would insert and then rotate 90 degrees to lock. The most common style was a cable that could thread through a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now revived this concept, releasing an adapter that can be installed on the corner or edge of a MacBook so you can attach a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece design that clamps onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has now added a version for the MacBook Neo, in addition to its existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It's important to stress that these locks have always offered a fairly low level of security—their purpose is simply to prevent someone from snatching your MacBook and running off in the few seconds while you're not looking. In smaller coffee shops, I'm happy to use one of these locks because I can still see my table when I walk to the counter for a refill of tea, but if I were to leave my MacBook completely out of sight, I would never rely on it.

The adapter doesn't come cheap at $70, and you'd still need to buy the lock itself separately. However, if you happen to have an old lock sitting in a drawer, it might be worth bringing it back into service.
